channel.title: Humanoids Daily
channel.description: We bring you the latest developments in robotics, with a special focus on humanoid robots and intelligent machines. From groundbreaking research to real-world applications, we cover the people, technologies, and innovations shaping the future of robotics.

item.title: AGIBOT Brings 300-Plus Robots to Chimelong Theme Park
item.description: AGIBOT and Chimelong have launched a robot deployment spanning performances, visitor guidance and hotel services at the existing Spaceship Park in Zhuhai, alongside a joint tourism research institute.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Skild AI’s S1 Learns Soccer Through More Than 140 Years of Simulated Self-Play
item.description: Skild reports real-world soccer play after more than 140 years of simulated self-play. Its published account details human-referenced drills before the goal-driven self-play stage.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: XPENG Lines Up Humanoid Suppliers Ahead of Year-End Production Target
item.description: XPENG says it has signed supplier agreements and is scheduling robot production after its first partner conference, as humanoid developers confront the challenge of securing consistent components at scale.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Vesoma Emerges From Stealth With a Humanoid Built to Learn
item.description: The European team behind the Kyle prototype reveals Vesoma, led by Synapticon and Easybrain co-founders, with former DeepMind research director Martin Riedmiller heading AI and its first Vesoma 1 units under construction.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Tesla App Contains Optimus Gen 3 Renders—Here’s What They Show
item.description: Optimus renders labeled gen3 first appeared in Tesla’s Android app on August 27, a four-build comparison shows. Higher-resolution versions arrived September 5, but the assets do not confirm final hardware or a working robot interface.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Tesla Looks to Berlin Factory Workers to Help Train Optimus
item.description: July reporting described plans for Grünheide workers to wear cameras for Optimus training. A new post revives the story, but the program’s current scale remains unclear.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Brett Adcock Says Humanoids Will Need More Data and Compute Than LLMs
item.description: Sharing Humanoids Daily’s interview clip, Figure’s CEO expands his four-stage roadmap and predicts hundreds of billions in spending to scale robot intelligence and manufacturing.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Apptronik CEO Warns America Is Missing the Parts to Build Humanoids
item.description: Jeff Cardenas singles out U.S. gear shortages and says actuators can account for 60% of robot parts costs, as Apptronik works to build domestic supply capacity.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Beijing Sets Humanoids a Rescue Challenge for October
item.description: An October competition will test robots on practical tasks and simulated hazards, with separate categories for remote operation and autonomous navigation.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: XPENG’s IRON Remembers Car Buyers in New Interaction Demo
item.description: XPENG shows IRON tracking speakers, switching languages and recalling customer preferences in a showroom-style R&D test, ahead of its planned store deployments.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: South Korea Plans Robot AI Push in 2027, Starting With Logistics
item.description: A planned 2027 program would combine robot AI research, a physical-data library and early postal and logistics trials. Its budget is still being finalized.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Robros Adds Full-Body Teleoperation to Its Korean Humanoid
item.description: Robros extends human control across IGRIS-C’s body as the Seoul startup reports early industrial sales and South Korea builds its humanoid ecosystem.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Boston Dynamics Opens Atlas Training Center at Hyundai’s Georgia Factory
item.description: The Georgia center is training Atlas for manufacturing tasks, ahead of Hyundai’s planned 2028 rollout. A tenfold expansion is scheduled for 2027.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: SoftBank Reportedly Agrees to Buy Marc Raibert’s Robotics Institute
item.description: The reported RAI acquisition would add robotics research capacity as Hyundai pursues SoftBank’s Boston Dynamics stake and SoftBank explores other humanoid investments.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Unitree Unveils Human-Sized Robot Hand Starting at $6,500
item.description: Unitree’s Dex5-S promises 22 degrees of freedom and backdrivable joints at human-hand scale. Its launch leaves key specifications and complete-task performance unverified.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: PrimeBOT Launches Personal Robots at 19,999 Yuan, Betting on Apps and Companionship
item.description: PrimeBOT opens Chinese sales of Q1 and T1, with October deliveries planned and a business model built around companionship, customization and future content revenue.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Faraday Future Expands Robot Lineup With $9,990 Master Mini
item.description: Faraday Future adds nine configurations across five robot models, while its Master Mini documentation points to Booster hardware behind the $9,990 education humanoid.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: IFR Counts 7,000 Humanoid Sales in 2025—Many for Research
item.description: Reuters reports IFR counted around 7,000 humanoid sales for industrial and professional use in 2025, highlighting the distinction between robot purchases and productive deployment.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Hyundai Eyes Czech Factory for Atlas Humanoid
item.description: Hyundai’s Nošovice plant is discussing Atlas with Boston Dynamics and headquarters, but a European deployment date remains unannounced.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: X Square’s Robot Starts Work at Lululemon’s Wuhan Warehouse
item.description: X Square says its QUANTA X1 Pro is handling parcels at lululemon’s new Wuhan distribution center, adding a named warehouse deployment to its logistics push.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Why Ningbo Matters to Tesla’s Optimus Ambitions
item.description: Tesla’s reported supplier audits put Ningbo’s automotive expertise in focus, as Georg Stieler highlights the Yangtze River Delta’s role in humanoid robotics.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Tesla App Code Hints at Optimus Charging and Home Integration
item.description: A decompilation of Tesla app 4.61.0 identifies Optimus charger IDs and an energy-site entry, suggesting software preparation without confirming a consumer launch.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: GPT-6 Astra Rarely Refused Unsafe Robot Commands in New Test
item.description: RoboHarm adds a safety test to Astra’s robotics results: 97 attempts and 60 completions across 100 unsafe-instruction trials, with only two safety refusals.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: 1X Aims to Ship 50,000 Robots—But Keeping Them Working Is the Test
item.description: Bernt Børnich outlines 1X’s shipment ambitions, a mix of home and enterprise deployments, and why he expects broader robot intelligence to gain ground in 2027.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Tesla Reportedly Begins New Optimus Supplier Audits in China
item.description: Reports point to a new round of Optimus supplier inspections in Ningbo, while company representatives confirm ongoing robotics work but stop short of verifying the latest visits.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Spirit AI Predicts a Robot-Brain Breakthrough in 2027
item.description: Co-founder Gao Yang expects a mid-2027 leap in robots’ ability to follow spoken instructions, while warning that useful household robots remain much further away.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: UBTECH Brings Walker C1 to Slovenia in Balkan Expansion Push
item.description: Walker C1’s Slovenian showcase follows a five-country distribution and integration agreement with Hiproject, adding to Chinese humanoid makers’ European presence.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Tesla’s Optimus Factory Nears a Steel-Frame Milestone in Texas
item.description: A new drone update shows steel and concrete work advancing at Tesla’s Texas robot factory, while production timing remains less certain than the construction progress.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Watney Raises $80 Million to Put Robots to Work in Data Centers
item.description: Watney’s Series A takes funding above $100 million as it targets data-center work, starting with cabling, and claims more than 99.99% reliability.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)

item.title: Lumos Says NexCore Can Teach Robots New Skills in Days
item.description: Lumos pitches NexCore as a faster route from task descriptions to factory-ready robot skills, citing Mitsubishi Electric applications but offering limited benchmark detail.
item.author: contact@humanoidsdaily.com (Humanoids Daily Staff)
